1	/// `POST /entries`'s four possible origins (`openapi.yaml:345-351`). This
2	/// story only ever produces [manual] (Boundaries: "source=manual for this
3	/// story") — the other three exist here already so the port
4	/// ([EntriesRepository.create]) doesn't need to change shape when Stories
5	/// 3.2/3.3 (audio/photo) and RF10 (chat) start passing them.
6	enum EntrySource { manual, audio, photo, chat }
7	
8	/// A saved journal entry — plain `{id, content, source, chatMessageId,
9	/// occurredAt, serverRevision, createdAt, updatedAt}` class, no `freezed`
10	/// (mirrors `AuthenticatedUser`: this feature has no need for the
11	/// union/copyWith machinery `Failure` uses). Boundaries: never a field
12	/// beyond this exact set — `tags`/`piiStatus`/`piiSpans`/`embeddingStatus`/
13	/// `mediaDurationSeconds` belong to later epics, not this story.
14	///
15	/// [occurredAt]/[createdAt]/[updatedAt] are kept as the backend's own ISO
16	/// 8601 strings rather than parsed into `DateTime` — nothing in this story
17	/// reads or formats them (Design Notes: the Hive box nothing reads from
18	/// yet), so parsing would add risk (a malformed string throwing) with no
19	/// behavior to justify it.
20	class Entry {
21	  const Entry({
22	    required this.id,
23	    required this.content,
24	    required this.source,
25	    required this.chatMessageId,
26	    required this.occurredAt,
27	    required this.serverRevision,
28	    required this.createdAt,
29	    required this.updatedAt,
30	  });
31	
32	  final String id;
33	  final String content;
34	  final EntrySource source;
35	
36	  /// Non-null only for a [EntrySource.chat]-sourced entry (RF10) — always
37	  /// `null` for this story's [EntrySource.manual] entries.
38	  final String? chatMessageId;
39	  final String occurredAt;
40	  final int serverRevision;
41	  final String createdAt;
42	  final String updatedAt;
43	
44	  @override
45	  bool operator ==(Object other) =>
46	      identical(this, other) ||
47	      (other is Entry &&
48	          other.id == id &&
49	          other.content == content &&
50	          other.source == source &&
51	          other.chatMessageId == chatMessageId &&
52	          other.occurredAt == occurredAt &&
53	          other.serverRevision == serverRevision &&
54	          other.createdAt == createdAt &&
55	          other.updatedAt == updatedAt);
56	
57	  @override
58	  int get hashCode => Object.hash(
59	    id,
60	    content,
61	    source,
62	    chatMessageId,
63	    occurredAt,
64	    serverRevision,
65	    createdAt,
66	    updatedAt,
67	  );
68	
69	  @override
70	  String toString() =>
71	      'Entry(id: $id, content: $content, source: $source, '
72	      'chatMessageId: $chatMessageId, occurredAt: $occurredAt, '
73	      'serverRevision: $serverRevision, createdAt: $createdAt, '
74	      'updatedAt: $updatedAt)';
75	}

3	part 'failure.freezed.dart';
4	
5	/// AD-3 — the one closed `Failure` hierarchy, exactly 14 subtypes: the 13
6	/// codes from `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md` plus the local-only
7	/// `malformedResponse` (client-side parse failure, never sent by the
8	/// backend). Never redefined or subset per feature; every repository method
9	/// returns `Either<Failure, T>` built from this type (RNF09).
10	///
11	/// `retryable` is derived here, once, from the 6 server `retryable:true`
12	/// codes (AD-4) — no other file re-decides which codes retry.
13	@freezed
14	sealed class Failure with _$Failure {
15	  const factory Failure.authExpired({required String message}) = AuthExpired;
16	  const factory Failure.authInvalid({required String message}) = AuthInvalid;
17	  const factory Failure.networkTimeout({required String message}) =
18	      NetworkTimeout;
19	  const factory Failure.networkOffline({required String message}) =
20	      NetworkOffline;
21	  const factory Failure.validation({required String message}) = Validation;
22	  const factory Failure.piiCheckFailed({required String message}) =
23	      PiiCheckFailed;
24	  const factory Failure.embeddingFailed({required String message}) =
25	      EmbeddingFailed;
26	  const factory Failure.aiGenerationTimeout({required String message}) =
27	      AiGenerationTimeout;
28	  const factory Failure.notFound({required String message}) = NotFound;
29	  const factory Failure.rateLimited({required String message}) = RateLimited;
30	  const factory Failure.exportEmptyPeriod({required String message}) =
31	      ExportEmptyPeriod;
32	  const factory Failure.payloadTooLarge({required String message}) =
33	      PayloadTooLarge;
34	  const factory Failure.ocrNoText({required String message}) = OcrNoText;
35	
36	  /// Local-only — the client's own parse-failure detection. `retryable` is
37	  /// hardcoded `false` for this subtype (AD-3).
38	  const factory Failure.malformedResponse({required String message}) =
39	      MalformedResponse;
40	
41	  const Failure._();
42	
43	  /// The 6 server `retryable:true` codes (AD-4). Every other code —
44	  /// including the local `malformedResponse` — is `false`.
45	  bool get retryable => switch (this) {
46	        NetworkTimeout() => true,
47	        NetworkOffline() => true,
48	        PiiCheckFailed() => true,
49	        EmbeddingFailed() => true,
50	        AiGenerationTimeout() => true,
51	        RateLimited() => true,
52	        AuthExpired() ||
53	        AuthInvalid() ||
54	        Validation() ||
55	        NotFound() ||
56	        ExportEmptyPeriod() ||
57	        PayloadTooLarge() ||
58	        OcrNoText() ||
59	        MalformedResponse() =>
60	          false,
61	      };
62	
63	  /// Maps a backend error `code` (`error-taxonomy.md`) to its `Failure`
64	  /// subtype. An unrecognized code (should never happen — the taxonomy is
65	  /// closed) falls back to [Failure.malformedResponse] rather than throwing,
66	  /// so no repository ever lets an unmapped error escape (RNF09).
67	  factory Failure.fromCode(String code, String message) => switch (code) {
68	        'AUTH_EXPIRED' => Failure.authExpired(message: message),
69	        'AUTH_INVALID' => Failure.authInvalid(message: message),
70	        'NETWORK_TIMEOUT' => Failure.networkTimeout(message: message),
71	        'NETWORK_OFFLINE' => Failure.networkOffline(message: message),
72	        'VALIDATION_ERROR' => Failure.validation(message: message),
73	        'PII_CHECK_FAILED' => Failure.piiCheckFailed(message: message),
74	        'EMBEDDING_FAILED' => Failure.embeddingFailed(message: message),
75	        'AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT' =>
76	          Failure.aiGenerationTimeout(message: message),
77	        'NOT_FOUND' => Failure.notFound(message: message),
78	        'RATE_LIMITED' => Failure.rateLimited(message: message),
79	        'EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD' => Failure.exportEmptyPeriod(message: message),
80	        'PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE' => Failure.payloadTooLarge(message: message),
81	        'OCR_NO_TEXT' => Failure.ocrNoText(message: message),
82	        _ => Failure.malformedResponse(message: message),
83	      };
84	}

3	/// Recording configuration
4	///
5	/// `encoder`: The audio encoder to be used for recording.
6	///
7	/// `bitRate`*: The audio encoding bit rate in bits per second.
8	///
9	/// `sampleRate`*: The sample rate for audio in samples per second.
10	///
11	/// `numChannels`: The numbers of channels for the recording.
12	/// 1 = mono, 2 = stereo.
13	///
14	/// `device`: The device to be used for recording. If null, default device
15	/// will be selected.
16	///
17	/// `autoGain`*: The recorder will try to auto adjust recording volume in a limited range.
18	///
19	/// `echoCancel`*: The recorder will try to reduce echo.
20	///
21	/// `noiseSuppress`*: The recorder will try to negates the input noise.
22	///
23	/// `*`: May not be considered on all platforms/formats.
24	class RecordConfig {
25	  /// The requested output format through this given encoder.
26	  final AudioEncoder encoder;
27	
28	  /// The audio encoding bit rate in bits per second if applicable.
29	  final int bitRate;
30	
31	  /// The sample rate for audio in samples per second if applicable.
32	  final int sampleRate;
33	
34	  /// The numbers of channels for the recording. 1 = mono, 2 = stereo.
35	  /// Most platforms only accept 2 at most.
36	  final int numChannels;
37	
38	  /// The device to be used for recording. If null, default device
39	  /// will be selected.
40	  final InputDevice? device;
41	
42	  /// The recorder will try to auto adjust recording volume in a limited range (if available on the device).
43	  ///
44	  /// Recording volume may be lowered by using this.
45	  final bool autoGain;
46	
47	  /// The recorder will try to reduce echo (if available on the device).
48	  ///
49	  /// Recording volume may be lowered by using this.
50	  final bool echoCancel;
51	
52	  /// The recorder will try to negates the input noise (if available on the device).
53	  ///
54	  /// Recording volume may be lowered by using this.
55	  final bool noiseSuppress;
56	
57	  /// Android specific configuration.
58	  final AndroidRecordConfig androidConfig;
59	
60	  /// iOS specific configuration.
61	  final IosRecordConfig iosConfig;
62	
63	  /// Recorder behaviour when audio is interrupted by another source.
64	  ///
65	  /// System alerts are ignored.
66	  /// Some other sources may not be detected (e.g. browser).
67	  ///
68	  /// Platforms: Android & iOS.
69	  final AudioInterruptionMode audioInterruption;
70	
71	  /// Useful for those who need finer data when streaming.
72	  ///
73	  /// Underlying implementations may adjust to other value or throw exception if under miminum size required.
74	  ///
75	  /// Platforms: Android, iOS, macOS & web.
76	  final int? streamBufferSize;
77	
78	  const RecordConfig({
79	    this.encoder = AudioEncoder.aacLc,
80	    this.bitRate = 128000,
81	    this.sampleRate = 44100,
82	    this.numChannels = 2,
83	    this.device,

85	    this.echoCancel = false,
86	    this.noiseSuppress = false,
87	    this.androidConfig = const AndroidRecordConfig(),
88	    this.iosConfig = const IosRecordConfig(),
89	    this.audioInterruption = AudioInterruptionMode.pause,
90	    this.streamBufferSize,
91	  });

5	
6	/// The epic's ONE new DI-singleton access point for device-level access
7	/// (AD-14) — `core/navigation/app_router.dart`'s `_redirect` reads
8	/// [currentStatus] before it reads `SessionRepository.currentStatus`
9	/// (Boundaries: "`_redirect` checks `VaultStatus` before `SessionStatus`").
10	/// Mirrors `features/auth/domain/repositories/session_repository.dart`'s
11	/// shape, except [currentStatus] is never nullable (see [VaultStatus]'s own
12	/// doc) and there is no `restoreSession`-equivalent boot call — the vault
13	/// is always [VaultStatus.locked] until a successful [authenticate] call.
14	abstract class VaultRepository {
15	  /// Broadcast stream of the current vault status. Unlike
16	  /// `SessionRepository.statusStream`, this always has a value from the
17	  /// moment the repository is constructed ([VaultStatus.locked]) — a late
18	  /// subscriber still immediately replays that cached value, same
19	  /// `Stream.multi` rationale as the session repository's own stream.
20	  Stream<VaultStatus> get statusStream;
21	
22	  /// The last status emitted on [statusStream], read synchronously —
23	  /// starts at [VaultStatus.locked] (never `null`, see [VaultStatus]'s own
24	  /// doc) and only a successful [authenticate] call ever flips it to
25	  /// [VaultStatus.unlocked].
26	  VaultStatus get currentStatus;
27	
28	  /// Triggers the OS biometric prompt (`local_auth`, `biometricOnly: true`
29	  /// — Boundaries: "never set `biometricOnly: false`"). Zero network calls
30	  /// (Boundaries: "Vault makes zero network calls"); never produces
31	  /// [Failure.authInvalid] (reserved for password login) — any failure here
32	  /// (OS declines, cancels, or throws `LocalAuthException`) maps to
33	  /// [Failure.malformedResponse] instead, and [currentStatus] stays
34	  /// [VaultStatus.locked]. Only a `true` result flips [currentStatus] to
35	  /// [VaultStatus.unlocked] and emits it on [statusStream].
36	  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> authenticate();
37	
38	  /// Story 2.2's biometric-failure fallback. No PIN-creation screen exists
39	  /// anywhere in `docs/input/` (Design Notes): the first call ever made to
40	  /// this method — regardless of which screen reached the keypad — stores
41	  /// [pin] as the vault's PIN and immediately succeeds; every later call
42	  /// compares [pin] against that stored value. A match (first-use or
43	  /// later) flips [currentStatus] to [VaultStatus.unlocked] and emits it on
44	  /// [statusStream], same as a successful [authenticate]. A mismatch never
45	  /// throws, never caps retries, and leaves [currentStatus] at
46	  /// [VaultStatus.locked] — [Failure.malformedResponse] is returned instead
47	  /// (RNF09), so the caller always has a retryable path, never a dead end.
48	  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> submitPin(String pin);
49	
50	  /// Releases the underlying stream resource. Wired as `get_it`'s
51	  /// `dispose:` callback on registration, so `resetCoreDependencies()`
52	  /// (`sl.reset()`) closes it instead of leaking a `StreamController` on
53	  /// every test teardown.
54	  Future<void> dispose();
55	}

8	/// Registers the `vault` feature into the project's single `get_it`
9	/// instance (`sl`) — mirrors `features/auth/auth_injection.dart`'s pattern.
10	/// Called from `setupCoreDependencies()` right after `registerAuthFeature()`
11	/// (Code Map).
12	void registerVaultFeature() {
13	  sl.registerLazySingleton<LocalAuthentication>(() => LocalAuthentication());
14	
15	  // The epic's ONE new DI-singleton access point for device-level access
16	  // (AD-14) — registered as a singleton so every consumer (the `/vault`
17	  // lock screen; `core/navigation/app_router.dart`'s redirect; `main.dart`)
18	  // shares the same `statusStream`, not a fresh instance each. `dispose:`
19	  // wires `VaultRepository.dispose()` into `get_it`'s own reset lifecycle,
20	  // so `resetCoreDependencies()` (`sl.reset()`) closes its
21	  // `StreamController` instead of leaking one on every test teardown.
22	  sl.registerLazySingleton<VaultRepository>(
23	    () => VaultRepositoryImpl(
24	      localAuthentication: sl<LocalAuthentication>(),
25	      // Already registered by `setupCoreDependencies()` (Code Map) — the
26	      // same singleton `SecureStorageAccessTokenProvider` uses for the
27	      // access/refresh tokens, now also holding the vault PIN (Story 2.2)
28	      // under its own distinct key.
29	      secureStorage: sl<FlutterSecureStorage>(),
30	    ),
31	    dispose: (repository) => repository.dispose(),
32	  );
33	}

input.message:
Implemented spec-3-2 (Audio Entry Capture & On-Device Transcription) fully, following its frozen Intent/Boundaries/I-O matrix as sole source of truth.

## What changed

**New capture-feature files:**
- `lib/features/capture/domain/services/mic_recorder.dart` — `MicRecorder` port + `MicRecording` value type (plain Dart, no `package:record` type crosses this boundary).
- `lib/features/capture/domain/services/audio_transcriber.dart` — `AudioTranscriber` port (`transcribe()` → `String?`, null = failure, never wrapped in `Failure`).
- `lib/features/capture/data/services/record_mic_recorder.dart` — wraps `package:record`'s `AudioRecorder` (16kHz mono wav, matches whisper's expected input), tracks start time itself since `stop()` only returns a path.
- `lib/features/capture/data/services/whisper_audio_transcriber.dart` — wraps `whisper_ggml`'s `WhisperController` (`WhisperModel.base`, `lang: 'pt'`, lazy `downloadModel`), catches any exception into `null`.
- `lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/audio_entry_cubit.dart` — `AudioEntryCubit` + sealed `AudioCaptureState` (`AudioIdle`/`AudioRecording`/`AudioProcessing`/`AudioTranscribed`/`AudioSaved`/`AudioError`), covering the full recording→processing→transcribed/error pipeline, retry semantics (re-request permission vs. re-transcribe vs. re-enable Salvar), cancel-on-tab-leave, and `save()` mirroring `TextEntryCubit`'s isClosed/no-double-submit guards.

**Entries feature** (`Entry`, `EntriesRepository.create`, `EntryDto` + generated `.g.dart`, `EntriesRemoteDataSource`, `EntriesRepositoryImpl`) all gained optional `int? mediaDurationSeconds`, sent/decoded only when non-null (`@JsonKey(includeIfNull: false)`), threaded end-to-end into the real Hive write-through.

**Wiring:** `pubspec.yaml` (+`record: ^6.0.0`, +`path_provider` promoted to a direct dependency since it's now imported directly), `capture_injection.dart` (registers `MicRecorder`/`AudioTranscriber` + the raw `AudioRecorder`/`WhisperController` plugin instances as lazy singletons, `AudioEntryCubit` as a factory like `TextEntryCubit`), `placeholder_screens.dart` (resolves and passes `AudioEntryCubit` to `InsertionModal.show`), `ios/Runner/Info.plist` (+`NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`, required by `record` on a real device).

**`insertion_modal.dart`** rewritten: `MultiBlocProvider` for both cubits, tab-switch listener now starts/cancels recording on Áudio enter/leave, a new `_AudioTab` (waveform via a rolling-amplitude-sample bar visualizer, mm:ss timer, stop control, editable transcribed-text field, error/retry views) replacing the old idle placeholder, and an `AudioSaved`→announce→pop listener mirroring `TextEntrySaved`'s.

## Verification
- `fvm flutter pub get` — resolved `record` cleanly (6 new transitive platform packages), no conflicts.
- `fvm flutter pub run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` — regenerated `entry_dto.g.dart` with the new field.
- `fvm flutter analyze` — **zero issues**.
- `fvm flutter test` — **448/448 passing** (up from 404 baseline), including:
  - `test/features/capture/presentation/cubit/audio_entry_cubit_test.dart` (24 tests, mocktail-mocked `MicRecorder`/`AudioTranscriber`/`EntriesRepository`).
  - `test/features/capture/data/services/record_mic_recorder_test.dart` + `whisper_audio_transcriber_test.dart` — mock the `record`/`whisper_ggml` plugin classes directly (same convention `vault_repository_impl_test.dart` uses for `LocalAuthentication`), never exercising real native plugins.
  - `test/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal_audio_test.dart` (new, 6 end-to-end widget tests against the real `InsertionModal`/`AudioEntryCubit`).
  - Entries-feature tests extended for `mediaDurationSeconds` (datasource send/decode, repository threading, real-Hive round-trip + null-omission).
  - One pre-existing test updated (`insertion_modal_test.dart`'s "tapping Áudio switches to its own idle placeholder" → now asserts the real functional pipeline, since Áudio is no longer a placeholder).

Also updated the spec's own frontmatter (`status: 'review'`) and its Tasks checklist (all boxes checked), plus `sprint-status.yaml`'s `3-2-...: review` entry, matching the project's documented dev→review workflow — left `deferred-work.md` untouched since that file's own convention is populated by a code-review pass, not the implementer.

## Notable risk/design decisions worth a reviewer's eye
1. **Widget-test infrastructure gotcha (now worked around, not a product bug):** calling `Cubit.close()` a second time on an already-closed `Cubit` that was wired through `BlocProvider`/widget listeners hangs indefinitely under `flutter_test` (confirmed empirically). `insertion_modal_audio_test.dart`'s `tearDown` now guards with `isClosed` checks.
